title: Chris Evans’ Doomsday Return Raises Questions About Steve Rogers’ Ending
excerpt:
The Encore edition of Endgame revisits Steve Rogers’ farewell.
A new critical argument questions what his return means for that conclusion.
body_md:
Avengers: Endgame closed the Infinity Saga in 2019 with two contrasting farewells. Tony Stark sacrificed his life to defeat Thanos, while Steve Rogers finally stepped away from the responsibilities that had defined his adult life. Their endings also answered the doubts each had expressed about the other in earlier Avengers films.

Tony proved willing to make the ultimate sacrifice, while Steve demonstrated his worthiness by wielding Mjolnir. His final dance with Peggy Carter fulfilled a promise dating back to Captain America: The First Avenger. The intimate scene offered emotional closure rather than another franchise tease.

According to the report on Avengers Endgame: Encore, that dance is now interrupted by a knock at the door. Loki appears, apparently bringing a warning connected to Doctor Doom. The original article argues that turning the farewell into a bridge to another adventure diminishes its emotional impact. That is a critical interpretation, not an established verdict on the upcoming movie.

Robert Downey Jr. is returning as Victor von Doom rather than Tony Stark, creating a different set of questions. Any connection between Doom and Stark remains uncertain, as does the precise identity of the Steve Rogers appearing in the new film. Suggestions that Steve could adopt the Nomad identity are speculative.

Doomsday could still reconcile its new story with the earlier ending, and Marvel has previously withheld important context from promotional material. The film is scheduled to open on December 18, 2026. Until then, whether Steve and Peggy retain their happy ending remains unresolved.
